checks: DESIGN DECISION, recorded because the plan did not make it: the mockup has three slots and the app has five surfaces. Placement chosen - left rail: vitals (StatsPanel) and risk; board slot: the map above the battle picture, divider and stored share unchanged; right rail: actions and the AiWorkerPanel; console row: scripts | transcript | experience strip. Nothing was dropped and no surface gained a second mount.

DESIGN DECISION: the transcript lives in the console row, not the board slot. D0(a) can be read as putting it in the slot, and the mockup's console row is built around it (.transcript is 30px|1fr|38px - a heading, a scroll, a command line). Two mounts of the transcript would be a fork whichever slot won, so it has exactly one.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED BY MEASURING: with fitColumns' slots mapped the obvious way (left rail -> room), the left rail rendered 431px wide at 1366x768 instead of 228, because `room` is the slot that absorbs unclaimed width. Turning the mapping around - board -> room, rails -> map/dash, each rail capped at its own want via mapGrowthMax/dashGrowthMax - fixed it without touching columns.ts.

BUG FOUND: pickReset resets to columns.ts's DEFAULT_*, which were the pre-frame numbers, so Reset widths would have given the vitals rail 620px. DEFAULT_MAP_W/DASH_W/ROOM_W are now defined AS SIDE_LEFT_W/SIDE_RIGHT_W/BOARD_MIN_W rather than as copies of their values, so there is one number per column. That required moving the frame-constant block above them in columns.ts - a const used before its declaration is a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError at module load, and the mover asserts every constant now precedes its use.

Storage keys bumped, not reused: drc.left-rail-width.v1, drc.board-slot-width.v1, drc.right-rail-width.v1, drc.map-height.v4. Each slot holds different content at a different size and a stored share is only a number; a v2 'room' share of 0.34 read as the new left rail is a 460px column of vitals. tools/build-player-data-doc.mjs caught the rename in both directions (undescribed keys AND orphaned descriptions) and its descriptions were updated.

INSTRUMENT DEFECT FOUND, and it invalidates the obvious way to do D5: ResizeObserver does not fire under the browser pane's viewport emulation. Proved rather than assumed - a freshly attached ResizeObserver of my own on <main> logged nothing (`roHits: []`) while main genuinely went 900 -> 1500 and innerWidth agreed. App.tsx reads hostW/hostH from a ResizeObserver, so resizing an already-loaded page leaves the component measuring a frozen width, and every rail number taken that way describes the size the page was LOADED at. The first three measurements were taken by resizing after loading at 1366 and were therefore unsound (they happened to give the same answer). All D5 numbers below were retaken by setting the viewport FIRST and loading the page fresh at each size. Whether a real OS window resize fires RO in WebView2 is untested here and is listed as not-checked, not as working.

D5 measurement, fresh load at each size, from getBoundingClientRect and scrollWidth/clientWidth. 1366x768: top bar 0,1366x48; left rail 0,228; board 236,872; right rail 1116,250; console row 0,1366x224; 1407 controls checked; 0 off-right; 0 off-bottom; body horizontal scroll 0; scrollHeight 768 == innerHeight.

D5 measurement 1920x1080: left rail 0,228; board 236,1426; right rail 1670,250; console row 0,1920x224; top bar 48 tall; 1407 controls checked; 0 off-right; 0 off-bottom; hscroll 0; scrollHeight 1080.

D5 measurement 2560x1440: left rail 0,228; board 236,2066; right rail 2310,250; console row 0,2560x224; top bar 48 tall; 1407 controls checked; 0 off-right; 0 off-bottom; hscroll 0; scrollHeight 1440. The rails hold at exactly the mockup's 228 and 250 at every size while the board takes all the surplus, which is the mapping fix above working.

D5's criterion was narrowed, and the reason is the point: 'every element's right <= innerWidth' counts anything inside a scroll container, and at 1366x768 the UNCHANGED pre-D4 layout produced 431 such 'violations' while being perfectly usable - a check that fires on a healthy layout says nothing about a broken one. The question columns.ts was actually written for is whether a CONTROL is off the edge with no scrollbar to reach it by, so the probe counts controls whose rect leaves the viewport AND which have no scrollable ancestor. 1407 controls is the denominator and it is printed every time.

The probe carries a positive control on every single run: a button positioned at innerWidth+60 in a non-scrolling parent is injected, measured, and removed. It was detected every time (offRight 1, worst entry 'CONTROL'), so each reported 0 is a fact about the layout rather than about a probe that stopped looking.
Pre-D4 baseline for comparison, same probe, same three sizes: 1389 controls checked, 0 unreachable at all three. So D4 did not introduce an unreachable control; it went from clean to clean.

frameFits is wired to the render and does collapse rails, verified live: fresh load at 800x700 -> both rails absent, board takes the full 800, hscroll 0. Fresh load at 1366 -> both rails present at 228/250. Importing the served module directly, frameFits(800,283) returns mustCollapse ['right','left'].
